findings.issue_text: header.scss .panel uses margin-left: auto for right alignment, but the flexbox() mixin also emits legacy display: -webkit-box/-moz-box, and the 2009 flexbox spec lacks auto-margin distribution, so old-syntax-only browsers render the panel next to the title instead of right-aligned (regression from float: right)

order() mixin forwards the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group (1-based, 0 invalid) and order (0-based), producing inconsistent ordering across engines for callers passing 0 or relying on absolute values
align-items() mixin passes flex-start/flex-end verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, whose legacy keywords are start/end, producing invalid declarations for those values
-ms-align-items in the align-items() mixin is not a real IE/Edge property; it is dead output adding bytes to every rule (the correct IE10 prefix -ms-flex-align is already present)
PR title describes the change as a performance optimization, but it is a float-to-flexbox layout refactor with no measurement or rationale, misrepresenting the change in history

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss .panel uses margin-left: auto for right alignment, but the flexbox() mixin also emits legacy display: -webkit-box/-moz-box, and the 2009 flexbox spec lacks auto-margin distribution, so old-syntax-only browsers render the panel next to the title instead of right-aligned (regression from float: right)

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss the layout for `.contents` is changed from float-based to flex-based: `.contents` now includes `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` no longer floats right, instead using `margin-left: auto` to push it to the end. However, the new `flexbox()` mixin emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` before the modern flex values. Browsers that only support the 2009 box model will pick `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box`, and that model does not support auto-margin distribution for alignment the way modern flex does. Since no `-webkit-box-pack`/spacer is added, `.panel` may not be pushed to the right in those legacy-only implementations, which is a real potential regression from the previous `float: right` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() mixin passes flex-start/flex-end verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, whose legacy keywords are start/end, producing invalid declarations for those values

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that directly assigns `$alignment` to legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties do not accept `flex-start`/`flex-end` (they use `start`/`end`), so calling `@include align-items(flex-start)` or `(...flex-end)` would emit invalid/ignored declarations for those prefixes. Even though the new call sites in this diff use `center` and `baseline` (which are valid), the mixin as introduced is incorrect for common flex values and can be verified from the CSS specs/legacy syntax behavior.
